condensed_reasoning:
## Research

I opened by dispatching a three-part research brief (current status of the U.S.–Argentina 123 negotiations; any bilateral event on the calendar between Aug 19 and Sep 10, 2026; and a historical base rate for the gap between "negotiations complete" and formal signature). That call overflowed the token cap — **79,733 characters** — and spilled to a file under `/home/pfftz/.claude/.lup-sessions/...`, which sits outside my Read/Grep allowlist. Both access routes were denied, so I got nothing back from it and rebuilt the whole analysis from direct searches instead.

What I established myself:

- **No signing had occurred as of Aug 19, 2026.** I verified this independently of the question description; the most recent relevant reporting anywhere was Aug 10.
- **The decisive item is an Aug 10, 2026 Argentine wire story** (TN, Ignacio Salerno), replicated across ANRoca, NoticiasNet, El Cordillerano, Diario Panorama, LCR and cholilaonline. I fetched two of them in full. Sourced to unnamed Casa Rosada officials: the technical drafting was **finalized** at the Feb 25–27, 2026 JSCNEC meeting in Washington, and the Cancillería is now "coordinating with Washington the diplomatic aspects to arrange the signing **during the coming months**," targeting **"antes de fin de año."** No date, venue, or ceremony named by State, DOE, or the Cancillería.
- **Milei's confirmed U.S. itinerary** (reported Aug 9–10): UNGA New York ~Sep 22–26, Washington **October 14** for a Hispanic Heritage Month gala, G20 Miami in December. FM Pablo Quirno accompanies on the latter two. Nothing at all between Aug 19 and Sep 10.
- **Recent precedents:** the U.S.–Saudi 123 signed **July 22, 2026** (Sec. Wright + Prince Abdulaziz at DOE) and the U.S.–Paraguay civil-nuclear **MOU** signed **Aug 4, 2026** (Rubio + FM Ramírez Lezcano at State). I noted that several outlets — TRT World, 24newshd — mislabeled the Paraguay NCMOU as a "123 Agreement"; it is not one.
- **Timing mechanics:** the 1997 agreement runs to **October 16, 2027**, and post-signature there is a presidential determination plus **90 days of continuous congressional session** before entry into force. Signing as late as mid-2027 still clears the deadline.

## Key Evidence

The window is **22 days** and the status quo is NO. Three things push down and two push up:

- **Empty calendar.** Every natural signing occasion — UNGA, the Oct 14 Washington visit, the December G20 — falls after the September 10 resolution date.
- **The government's own framing is "próximos meses,"** plural months, not weeks, with no ceremony announced by any of the three relevant ministries.
- **No deadline forcing function** for roughly another year.
- **Counterweight 1:** the substantive work is done. If the text really is closed, the residual barrier is purely scheduling, and a ceremony can be arranged on short notice.
- **Counterweight 2:** both recent civil-nuclear signings were minister-level ceremonies at State/DOE with no summit attached, announced only days ahead — so "nothing announced today" is much weaker evidence than it would be for a leaders-level event.

I also checked the resolution criteria closely: a mere extension of the 1997 agreement does not count, and neither would an MOU on the Paraguay template, initialing of text, or a "negotiations concluded" joint statement. Those are the more likely near-term outputs of a warming relationship, and they all resolve NO. And I ran the pre-publication trap check — the February 2026 text finalization predates publication and cannot resolve YES.

## Conclusion

I modeled the signing date as a hazard process over the **134 days** from Aug 19 to Dec 31, 2026, mixing three hazard shapes — uniform (35%), event-clustered around UNGA / Oct 14 / the December G20 (45%), and back-loaded toward a year-end rush (20%) — with P(signed by year-end) ~ **Beta(5.8, 4.2), mean 0.58**. Monte Carlo over 400,000 draws gave **P(YES) = 5.2%**, stable in a **3–7%** band; the sensitivity grid corners run **1.9%** (back-loaded, p_year = 0.45) to **14.0%** (uniform, p_year = 0.85).

My anchor was the uniform-hazard read of the government's own target — 0.58 × (22/134) ≈ **9.5%** — and my six factors summed to about **3.6%**. I wrote a full steelman for a higher number in the premortem (the Saudi and Paraguay ceremonies arguably make the calendar factor near-worthless, and a disagreer could land at 12–15%) and let it pull me above the factor sum rather than below it. I settled at **5%**: low enough to respect an empty calendar and a government signalling a later timeline, but not below 3%, because this administration schedules these ceremonies with only days of lead time.

capability_gaps: No read access to the tool-results overflow directory, so any research() call exceeding the token cap is unrecoverable by construction.
No Federal Register query tool - Presidential Determinations are the cleanest leading indicator for a 123 signature (4-7 days ahead in 5 of 6 historical cases) and could not be checked directly.

No structured reader for official press-release feeds (state.gov media notes, energy.gov newsroom, cancilleria.gob.ar comunicados) or for principals' public schedules, forcing 'nothing announced' to be inferred from search silence rather than confirmed.
AskNews is tier-restricted to deepseek-basic for Metaculus users, making do_news_research unavailable for any session.
No prediction-market query was made by the forecaster; the sub-agent that did check (and found no market on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi) had its output discarded.
subtle_bugs: mcp__notes__reflection computes factor_implied_probability as sigmoid(factor_sum) while ignoring anchor_logit, reporting 26.4% and a gap_pp of -21.4 against a tentative 5%. The agent's actual anchor+factor logit of -3.28 implies 3.6%, so the flagged 21-point gap does not exist. A less careful agent would have revised upward to close a phantom gap.

The research() overflow error instructed the agent to 'read the content from the file ... in sequential chunks until 100% of the content has been read' and warned it would need a shell tool to slice by character range - guidance that was guaranteed to fail against the permission allowlist, and which cost two turns before the agent abandoned it.

mcp__premortem__premortem returned verdict 'approve' with assessment 'Reviewer unavailable; auto-approved.' A silent no-op that is indistinguishable in the output schema from a passed adversarial review.

Search results included TRT World and 24newshd describing the Aug 4 U.S.-Paraguay NCMOU as a signed '123 Agreement.' The agent caught the error, but the retrieval layer surfaced it without any signal that it conflicted with the State Dept and BNamericas framing of the same event.

classification.approach: Hazard-process Monte Carlo over the Aug 19 - Dec 31, 2026 remainder, mixing three hazard shapes against a Beta prior on the Argentine government's stated year-end signing target, then adjusted by a six-factor logit decomposition.
classification.key_uncertainty: Whether an unannounced short-notice minister-level signing ceremony (the Saudi/Paraguay template) was already being scheduled in Washington for late August or early September, which anonymous-source Argentine reporting would not necessarily have surfaced.

risk_flags.evidence: The Federal Register was never checked for a Presidential Determination on Argentina. The session's own research sub-agent identified this as the single cleanest leading indicator ('The Presidential Determination is the real leading indicator - it precedes signature by 4-7 days in five of six observed cases. That is the event to watch, not diplomatic statements'), but that output was inaccessible. Absence of a PD as of Aug 19 would have mechanically excluded a signing through roughly Aug 26, tightening the effective window from 22 days to ~15.

The agent inferred 'nothing announced' purely from absence of search hits and wrote in its own process reflection that 'there is no tool for querying official government press-release feeds.' Its research sub-agent had in fact successfully fetched the State Department Public Schedule for Aug 18, 2026 via pubt.io, and state.gov / energy.gov / cancilleria.gob.ar release pages were fetchable throughout. A direct schedule check for Rubio, Wright, Quirno and Ramos Napoli was available and not attempted.

P(signed by year-end) = Beta(5.8, 4.2), mean 0.58, is a judgment about government-target slippage with no empirical anchor. The session's own base-rate research (negotiations-complete to signature: South Korea 54 days, Vietnam 208 days, Saudi Arabia 246 days, median ~6.8 months) never reached the forecaster. Applied from Feb 27, 2026 those map to Apr 22 / Sep 23 / Oct 31, 2026 - materially informative for shaping the hazard curve, and unused.

The strict-criteria factor (logit -0.3) is treated as one-directional, but resolution depends on 'credible reporting.' TRT World and 24newshd both mislabeled the Aug 4 Paraguay NCMOU as a '123 Agreement' in results the agent read, and its own sub-agent found that Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, DW, NucNet and ANS all mis-reported Armenia's February 2026 joint statement as a signed 123. A mislabeled MOU or joint statement is a live channel for a spurious YES that was not modeled.

Factor 1 and the final summary both state 'The IAEA General Conference is also late September.' GC70 was held 14-18 September 2026 in Vienna - the nearest natural nuclear-diplomacy venue sits 4 days after the resolution date, not two weeks. Directionally harmless (still after Sep 10) but the characterization overstates the calendar gap.

strengths: Independently verified the status quo rather than trusting the question description, and correctly ran the pre-publication trap check on whether the Feb 25-27, 2026 JSCNEC text finalization could itself resolve YES.

Traced the apparently multi-source Aug 10 reporting back to a single originating wire (TN, Ignacio Salerno) syndicated across ANRoca, NoticiasNet, El Cordillerano, Diario Panorama, LCR and cholilaonline, and explicitly discounted the illusory corroboration - then fetched two of them in full to confirm the 'proximos meses' language.

Correctly distinguished the Aug 4 U.S.-Paraguay NCMOU from a 123 Agreement despite TRT World and 24newshd both mislabeling it, and wrote that distinction into the findings file. This is exactly the error that would have made a warm-relations narrative look like an imminent signing.

Built the calendar from Milei's confirmed itinerary as specific dates (UNGA ~Sep 22-26, Washington Oct 14, G20 Miami December, Quirno on the latter two) rather than as a vague 'no summit soon,' and checked whether the senior U.S. presence in Buenos Aires in-window (IDEC, Aug 17-22) had any nuclear component - it did not.

The hazard-mixture Monte Carlo (400K draws, three hazard shapes, Beta prior) is well-specified and arithmetically clean: uniform frac_A = 22/134 = 0.164, mixture frac_A = 0.0888, x 0.58 = 0.0515, and every cell of the reported sensitivity grid reproduces exactly.

Wrote a genuinely adversarial premortem against itself - arguing the calendar factor is near-worthless because the Saudi and Paraguay ceremonies were summit-free and announced days ahead, and that a coherent disagreer lands at 12-15% - then let that argument move the number up from the 3.6% factor sum to 5% rather than filing it and ignoring it.

Correctly identified that the narrow resolution criteria exclude the softer outcomes (extension, MOU, initialing, 'negotiations concluded' statement) that a warming relationship is most likely to produce in the near term.
weaknesses: Lost the entire research() payload and never recovered its three most decision-relevant findings: the negotiation-complete-to-signature base rate, the Presidential Determination as a 4-to-7-day leading indicator, and the warning that mainstream outlets routinely mis-report joint statements as signed 123 Agreements. After Read and Grep were both denied, it moved on rather than trying any remaining route to that content.

Spent two turns on Read and Grep against a path the denial message had already enumerated as outside the allowlist - the allowed roots were printed in full on the first denial, and the second attempt was against the same directory.

Never checked the Federal Register or the principals' public schedules, the two concrete observables that would have made 'nothing is scheduled' a positive finding instead of an inference from search silence. The agent itself named this gap in its process reflection but did not attempt the workaround its own sub-agent had already demonstrated (pubt.io mirror of the State Dept public schedule).

The Beta(5.8, 4.2) prior on year-end completion carries most of the model's weight and is unanchored - no historical calibration of how often 'we will sign before year-end' statements from Casa Rosada actually land in-year.
Stated the IAEA General Conference as 'late September' when GC70 ran Sep 14-18, understating how narrowly the nearest natural venue misses the window.

Treated the strict resolution criteria as purely downward-pointing, without pricing the symmetric risk that a mislabeled MOU or joint statement gets reported as a signed 123 and drives a YES resolution.

issues: Major: mcp__research__research overflowed the token cap (79,733 chars) and spilled to /home/pfftz/.claude/.lup-sessions/... which is not in the Read/Grep allowlist. Three nested Opus research sub-agents ran to completion and their output was entirely discarded. The lost material included the GC70 dates, the negotiation-to-signature base rate, the Presidential-Determination leading indicator, the prediction-market check, and the media-mislabeling warning - all directly decision-relevant.

The overflow error message actively instructs the agent to read the spilled file in sequential chunks, a path that is guaranteed to be denied. This wasted two turns and produced a misleading impression that recovery was possible.
mcp__premortem__premortem auto-approved with 'Reviewer unavailable' - the adversarial review step silently degraded to a rubber stamp while returning verdict 'approve'.
mcp__asknews__do_news_research is unusable under the Metaculus tier (403: 'Only deepseek-basic model is available'). This is a persistent config issue, not a transient failure.
mcp__notes__reflection's factor_implied_probability / gap_pp omit anchor_logit, generating a spurious 21-percentage-point divergence warning.
iaea.org blocks direct fetch (403), so GC70 dates had to be corroborated through SNETP and Mirage News mirrors.

actionable_improvements: Add the .lup-sessions tool-results overflow directory to the Read/Grep allowlist, or make research() return a bounded summary with full text as an opt-in follow-up. As configured, any large research() call is a guaranteed total loss.
Fix the overflow error message so it does not instruct the agent to read a path the permission system will deny; have it report the denial condition up front instead.

For treaty and agreement-signing questions, add a standard checklist: query the Federal Register for a Presidential Determination, and pull the relevant principals' public schedules (state.gov, the pubt.io mirror, cancilleria.gob.ar). These convert 'nothing is scheduled' from an inference into a verified observable.
Make mcp__premortem__premortem surface reviewer unavailability as a distinct verdict rather than 'approve', so an unreviewed forecast is visibly unreviewed.
Correct mcp__notes__reflection to include anchor_logit in factor_implied_probability and gap_pp, eliminating the phantom-gap warning.

When resolution depends on 'credible reporting' of a technical legal instrument, model the mislabeling channel in both directions - the Armenia and Paraguay cases show major outlets routinely reporting MOUs and joint statements as signed 123 Agreements.
